subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold it into the broader Control UI notification architecture, or leave shell-originated alerts to plugin/external delivery paths?
rationale: The feature is absent but would create a new shell-facing admin capability that affects Gateway authorization scope, visible UI interruption policy, payload sanitization, rate limits, and overlap with existing Web Push/toast work.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Notification Architecture
options.body: Make #20237 own the UI architecture and supersede this issue only after it explicitly covers shell/admin broadcast semantics.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject the core command and document the supported plugin, channel, or Web Push workaround if maintainers decide shell-originated alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main and history signal across the CLI, Gateway broadcast, and security-sensitive event-scope paths that need the product/API decision.
